Adobe Inc. DROPPED on the OWNER'S OWN JUDGMENT, before any section 5 run and outside the framework's machinery -- the other names were all read first, this one was not. NOT VERIFIED: no search was made before ruling, and no figure, date or source supports any claim below. That is a deliberate departure from FRAMEWORK section 0 rule 1 and is recorded rather than hidden. The thesis: Adobe owned creative software because professionals had no alternative; the dominance came from lock-in rather than from the products improving, and the revenue comes from raising the price of software the user can never own. Two things sharpen it -- cancellation is made deliberately hard and the fines for that are cheaper than the revenue it protects, and a company whose product is winning does not need to make leaving difficult; and no revolutionary product in five years, with Photoshop and Premiere barely changed in ten, while Firefly is incremental and is not the best AI, so their own AI cannibalises their own product without leading. Why this is not simply another Oracle: AI now lets people create without them, which is the alternative that did not exist before -- a company can coast on lock-in for decades when customers have nowhere to go. RE-ENTRY: deploying the capital into something genuinely different, as Oracle did with cloud rather than staying in its own category; buying competitors inside creative software is not that, and there is no sign of it today. Full reasoning and the falsifiers in reference/growth-views/ADBE.md.
